q: Choose the word that is nearest in meaning (synonym) to the underlined word:\nThe manager gave a METICULOUS explanation of the new financial policy.
exp: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning (antonym) to the underlined word:\nThe minister was applauded for his CANDID assessment of the economic situation.
exp: 'Candid' means truthful and straightforward; its opposite is deceptive or evasive.

q: Choose the correct option to fill the gap:\nNeither the teacher nor the students present at the meeting yesterday.
exp: With 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('the students' is plural => were).

q: Choose the correct option to fill the gap:\nThe committee submitted report to the governing council this morning.
exp: 'Committee' acting as a collective unit takes the singular possessive pronoun 'its'.

q: Choose the correct option to complete the conditional sentence:\nIf she hard, she would have passed the examination.
exp: Past counterfactual conditional (Third conditional) requires 'had + past participle' in the if-clause.

q: Identify the figure of speech in the expression: 'The angry waves swallowed the small fishing boat.'
exp: Attributing human traits ('angry', 'swallowed') to inanimate sea waves is personification.

q: Choose the word with the same vowel sound as the one in bold: b**ir**d /ɜː/
exp: 'Bird' and 'word' both contain the central long vowel /ɜː/.

q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the underlined letter: **ph**ilosophy
exp: 'ph' in philosophy represents the voiceless labiodental fricative /f/, as in 'fame'.

q: Choose the option that best explains the idiom:\n'The new clerk decided to **let the cat out of the bag**.'
exp: To 'let the cat out of the bag' means to reveal confidential information, often unintentionally.

q: Choose the correct preposition:\nThe young scholar was acquitted the charges of examination malpractice.
exp: The standard prepositional collocation with 'acquit' is 'acquit someone of an offense'.

q: Choose the word with the primary stress on the first syllable:
exp: 'COM-for-ta-ble' carries primary stress on the initial syllable.

q: Choose the option that correctly completes the tag question:\nYou have not seen the principal today, ?
exp: A negative statement takes an affirmative tag: 'have not seen' => 'have you?'.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to EPHEMERAL:
exp: 'Ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time; its antonym is 'permanent'.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to EXONERATE:
exp: To exonerate is to officially declare someone not guilty or blame-free (absolve).

q: Choose the correct modal auxiliary:\nYou finish the assignment before the deadline tomorrow; it is mandatory.
exp: 'Must' expresses mandatory obligation.

q: Select the correctly punctuated sentence:
a: Although he was exhausted, he completed the project on time.
b: Although he was exhausted he completed, the project on time.
c: Although, he was exhausted he completed the project on time.
d: Although he was exhausted; he completed the project on time.
exp: A subordinate clause at the beginning of a sentence is set off by a comma.

q: Choose the word that has a different stress pattern from the others:
exp: Democracy is stressed on the 2nd syllable (de-MOC-ra-cy); the others are on the 3rd syllable.

q: Choose the correct spelling:
exp: Accommodate is spelled with double 'c' and double 'm'.

q: Choose the correct form:\nTen kilometres too far to walk on foot in this heat.
exp: Expressions of distance, time, and money viewed as a single unit take singular verbs.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to UBIQUITOUS:
exp: 'Ubiquitous' means present, appearing, or found everywhere (omnipresent).

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: ABHOR.
exp: To abhor means to regard with extreme repugnance or hatred.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: AMELIORATE.
exp: To ameliorate is to make a bad situation more bearable or better.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: ANOMALY.
a: Deviation from the norm or irregularity
exp: An anomaly is something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: AUDACIOUS.
exp: Audacious implies a bold disregard for normal constraints or danger.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: BELLIGERENT.
exp: Belligerent means combative or eager to fight.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: CACOPHONY.
a: A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds
exp: Cacophony refers to a loud, grating, harsh dissonance.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: DEARTH.
a: A scarcity or lack of something
exp: A dearth is a state of shortage, inadequacy, or famine.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: DELETERIOUS.
exp: Deleterious describes something harmful, toxic, or injurious.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: DIFFIDENT.
a: Modest or shy because of a lack of self-confidence
exp: Diffident means hesitant in acting or speaking through lack of self-assurance.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: ENERVATE.
a: Cause someone to feel drained of energy; weaken
exp: To enervate is to sap the physical, mental, or moral vitality of someone.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: EQUIVOCAL.
a: Open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous
exp: Equivocal language is deliberately vague or capable of differing interpretations.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: FASTIDIOUS.
a: Very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail
exp: Fastidious means excessively particular, critical, or demanding.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: GARRULOUS.
a: Excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters
exp: Garrulous means pointlessly or annoyingly loquacious.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: GREGARIOUS.
exp: Gregarious individuals enjoy being around other people in social groups.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: HACKNEYED.
a: Lacking significance through having been overused; cliché
exp: Hackneyed phrases or ideas have grown stale through constant repetition.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: IMPETUOUS.
a: Acting or done quickly and without thought or care
exp: Impetuous behavior is rash, impulsive, and unthinking.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: LACONIC.
exp: Laconic speech is terse, pithy, and brief to the point of seeming blunt.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: MAGNANIMOUS.
a: Generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival
exp: Magnanimous describes high-minded, noble generosity and grace in victory.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: NEFARIOUS.
exp: Nefarious deeds are reprehensibly evil or iniquitous.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the capitalized word: OBDURATE.
a: Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course
exp: Obdurate means unmoved by persuasion, pity, or tender feelings.

q: Neither the director nor his assistants _______ willing to sign the requisition voucher.
exp: In neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject ("assistants" -> were).

q: The committee _______ divided in their opinions regarding the zoning formula.
exp: A collective noun takes a plural verb when individual members act independently or hold divergent views.

q: One of the armed robbery suspects _______ escaped from lawful custody yesterday.
exp: The subject is singular ("One"), requiring the singular verb "has".

q: The commissioner, alongside his principal aides, _______ arrived at the venue.
exp: Parenthetical phrases like "alongside" do not affect the singular subject ("commissioner" -> has).

q: Bread and butter _______ served as our regular breakfast in boarding school.
exp: Compound subjects referring to a single collective food item take a singular verb.

q: Three-quarters of the arable farmland _______ been devastated by the flash flood.
exp: Fractions take singular verbs when modifying singular or uncountable nouns ("farmland" -> has).

q: More than one candidate _______ disqualified for possessing prohibited electronic gadgets.
exp: "More than one" is syntactically followed by a singular noun and singular verb.

q: Many a brilliant graduate _______ roaming the streets in search of employment.
exp: "Many a" takes a singular countable noun and requires a singular verb.

q: Neither of the political parties _______ ready to accept the tribunal ruling.
exp: "Neither of" takes a singular verb in standard formal English.

q: Economics _______ considered an essential prerequisite for admission into the faculty of business.
exp: Academic disciplines ending in -s take singular verbs.

q: The jury _______ unanimously delivered its verdict before the presiding trial judge.
exp: When a collective noun acts as a unified body, it takes a singular verb and pronoun ("its").

q: The rich also _______ their own peculiar family challenges and emotional burdens.
exp: Adjectives functioning as plural collective nouns take plural verbs.

q: Ten million naira _______ demanded by the kidnappers as ransom money.
exp: Sums of money and periods of time regarded as a lump sum take singular verbs.

q: Either the commercial driver or his conductors _______ responsible for the fare hike.
exp: In either...or constructions, the verb agrees with the closer subject ("conductors" -> were).

q: Not only the governor but also his commissioners _______ present at the groundbreaking ceremony.
exp: In not only...but also, the verb agrees with the adjacent subject ("commissioners" -> were).

q: The baggage _______ left unattended at the departure lounge for several hours.
exp: "Baggage" is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

q: The police _______ arrested three notorious kidnap kingpins along the interstate highway.
exp: "Police" is a plural collective noun and takes a plural verb.

q: The scissors _______ placed neatly inside the upper drawer of the technician desk.
exp: Two-part instruments (scissors, tongs, shears) take plural verbs unless preceded by "a pair of".

q: A pair of trousers _______ purchased from the boutique yesterday evening.
exp: "A pair of" makes the grammatical subject singular ("was").

q: Every teacher and student in the auditorium _______ given a commemorative anniversary badge.
exp: Nouns preceded by "every" or "each" take singular verbs even when coordinated with "and".

q: The belligerent posture of the warlord scuttled the international peace negotiations.
exp: "Belligerent" means hostile, combative, or aggressive.

q: The government enacted stringent regulations to curb illicit financial flows across borders.
exp: "Stringent" means strict, precise, and rigorous.

q: His ephemeral fame vanished shortly after the talent exhibition concluded.
exp: "Ephemeral" means lasting for a very short duration; transient.

q: The witness gave an equivocal testimony that perplexed the defense counsels.
exp: "Equivocal" means open to multiple interpretations; ambiguous.

q: The managing director praised the tenacity of the marketing division during the economic recession.
exp: "Tenacity" means the quality of being persistent and resolute.

q: The philanthropic gesture of the oil magnate provided scholarships for hundreds of indigent scholars.
exp: "Philanthropic" means benevolent, generous, or charitable.

q: The prosecutor presented incontrovertible forensic evidence that sealed the conviction.
exp: "Incontrovertible" means undeniable or indisputable.

q: She had a meticulous approach to financial bookkeeping, ensuring zero discrepancies.
exp: "Meticulous" means showing great attention to detail; painstaking.

q: The pervasive stench from the open refuse dump contaminated the entire residential estate.
exp: "Pervasive" means spreading widely throughout an area.

q: The candidate gave an audacious address demanding fundamental systemic constitutional reforms.
exp: "Audacious" means showing a willingness to take bold risks.

q: The speaker was lauded for his eloquent presentation at the Pan-African youth summit.
exp: "Eloquent" means fluent, expressive, and persuasive in speaking.

q: His ostentatious display of affluence attracted public reproach during the economic austerity.
exp: "Ostentatious" means vulgar or pretentious display designed to impress.

q: The tribunal ruled that the company showed culpable negligence leading to the collapse.
exp: "Culpable" means deserving blame; guilty.

q: The politician made a candid confession about his past financial misdeeds.
exp: "Candid" means truthful, straightforward, and frank.

q: The ancient parchment was remarkably legible despite centuries of storage.
exp: "Legible" means clear enough to be read.

q: The judge commended the defendant for his candid submission in the courtroom. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Candid" means frank; its antonym is deceitful or insincere.

q: The minister gave an impromptu address at the youth symposium. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Impromptu" means done without preparation; its opposite is rehearsed.

q: The barren terrain yielded virtually no agricultural produce during the extended drought. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Barren" means unproductive; its antonym is fertile.

q: Her tacit agreement to the partnership terms surprised her business associates. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Tacit" means implied; its antonym is explicit.

q: The general was notorious for his ruthless suppression of dissenting military factions. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Ruthless" means without pity; its antonym is merciful.

q: The corporation recorded colossal financial losses in the final quarter. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Colossal" means extremely large; its antonym is negligible.

q: The island lived in pristine ecological conditions prior to commercial oil exploration. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Pristine" means in original pure condition; its antonym is polluted.

q: The commandant issued a mandatory directive for all active personnel to muster. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Mandatory" means compulsory; its antonym is optional.

q: His arrogant disposition alienated several of his longstanding associates. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Arrogant" means conceited; its opposite is humble.

q: The supreme court declared the disputed decree null and void. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Null and void" means invalid; its opposite is valid.

q: The diplomat handled the volatile territorial dispute with extraordinary equanimity. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Equanimity" means mental calmness; its antonym is agitation.

q: The theologian held orthodox views on liturgical worship and doctrinal canons. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Orthodox" means conforming to established doctrine; its antonym is heterodox.

q: The apprentice was commended for being industrious throughout the technical attachment. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Industrious" means hardworking; its opposite is indolent or lazy.

q: The demagogue delivered an inflammatory address that incited communal skirmishes. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Inflammatory" means arousing violent passions; its antonym is soothing.

q: The treasurer maintained a parsimonious budget during the financial crisis. (Opposite in meaning)
exp: "Parsimonious" means excessively frugal; its antonym is extravagant.

q: The union representatives decided to call _______ the general strike after reaching an agreement.
exp: "To call off" means to cancel an event or strike action.

q: The student refused to abide _______ the hostel disciplinary regulations.
exp: The verb "abide" in the sense of complying with rules collocates with "by".

q: She found it stressful to cope _______ both rigorous graduate coursework and full-time employment.
exp: The correct English idiom is "cope with", not "cope up with".

q: The forensic auditor stumbled _______ confidential ledger entries detailing the fraud.
exp: To find unexpectedly is to "stumble on/upon".

q: The senate committee promised to look _______ the complaints lodged by the student union.
exp: "To look into" means to investigate thoroughly.

q: The defendant was completely exonerated _______ any complicity in the treasonous conspiracy.
exp: One is exonerated "from" or "of" criminal charges.

q: His sudden resignation from the cabinet came as a bolt from the _______ to political analysts.
exp: "A bolt from the blue" means a sudden, unexpected event.

q: The corrupt official used his public position to feather his own nest. This means he:
exp: "To feather one's nest" means to make oneself wealthy dishonestly through public office.

q: The prime minister decided to take the bull by the horns by dissolving the rebellious parliament. This means he:
exp: "To take the bull by the horns" means to deal with a crisis directly and courageously.

q: When interrogated under oath, the accomplice decided to spill the beans. This means he:
exp: "To spill the beans" means to reveal confidential information or secrets.

q: He still has a chip on his shoulder regarding his dismissal from the academy. This means he:
a: harbors an enduring grievance and resentment
exp: Having a "chip on one's shoulder" means harboring a grudge or bitter grievance.

q: After receiving the national literary award, she was cautioned not to rest on her _______.
exp: "To rest on one's laurels" means to be satisfied with past achievements and make no further effort.

q: The procurement tender was rejected because it failed to conform _______ statutory guidelines.
exp: "Conform to" or "conform with" indicates adherence; "to" is standard here.

q: The accountant was convicted of conniving _______ external syndicates to forge bank drafts.
exp: One connives "with" a co-conspirator to commit fraud.

q: The reckless driver was formally charged _______ vehicular manslaughter in the magistrate court.
exp: In legal jurisprudence, an accused person is "charged with" an offense.

q: Which of the following words contains the identical vowel sound to that in "key"?
exp: "Quay" is pronounced /ki:/, which shares the long vowel /i:/ found in "key".

q: Identify the word sharing the same central long vowel sound as "b_ir_d":
exp: The long central vowel in "bird" /bɜ:d/ is identical to that in "fern" /fɜ:n/.

q: Which of the following words contains the diphthong /aɪ/?
exp: "Eye" is pronounced /aɪ/, matching "my", "pie", and "high".

q: Identify the word that contains the voiceless dental fricative sound /θ/:
exp: "Thin" begins with the voiceless dental fricative /θ/, whereas "this" and "then" have voiced /ð/.

q: Which of the following words contains the voiced dental fricative sound /ð/?
exp: "Feather" contains the voiced dental fricative /ð/, whereas the others have voiceless /θ/.

q: In which of the following words is the initial consonant letter "p" silent?
exp: The letter "p" is silent in "psalm" /sɑ:m/, as well as in "psychology".

q: In which of the following words is the letter "b" silent in pronunciation?
exp: The letter "b" is silent before "t" in "doubt" and after "m" in "tomb".

q: Identify the word that contains the short vowel sound /æ/:
exp: "Cat" has the short front open vowel /æ/, whereas "father" has /ɑ:/.

q: Which of the following words rhymes with "cough"?
exp: "Cough" is pronounced /kɒf/ and rhymes perfectly with "off" /ɒf/.

q: Identify the word that contains the sound /tʃ/ as in "chair":
exp: The "t" in "nature" is pronounced /tʃ/ (/ˈneɪtʃər/).

q: Which syllable receives primary stress in the noun "CON-DUCT" (behavior)?
exp: Two-syllable words functioning as nouns generally take stress on the first syllable.

q: Which syllable receives primary stress in the verb "con-DUCT" (to direct or lead)?
exp: Two-syllable words functioning as verbs generally take stress on the second syllable.

q: In the word "PHOTOGRAPHY", on which syllable does the primary stress fall?
exp: Words ending in "-graphy" take primary stress on the antepenultimate syllable.

q: In the word "DEMOCRATIC", which syllable receives the primary stress?
exp: Words ending in "-ic" take primary stress on the syllable immediately preceding the suffix.

q: In the word "EDUCATION", which syllable receives the primary stress?
exp: Words ending in "-tion" receive primary stress on the penultimate syllable.

q: The witness swore an oath on the Holy Book to tell the truth. The underlined expression functions as an adverbial of:
exp: "On the Holy Book" indicates the location or medium upon which the oath was taken.

q: If he _______ worked harder during the term, he would have passed the promotional examination.
exp: Third conditional clauses express past counterfactuals using "had + past participle".

q: I would rather you _______ the assignment before Friday evening.
exp: "Would rather" followed by a subject takes a past subjunctive verb form to express present or future preference.

q: It is high time we _______ for the examination hall.
exp: The structure "It is high time" takes the past subjunctive form of the verb.

q: Scarcely had the referee blown the whistle _______ the jubilant supporters invaded the pitch.
exp: "Scarcely" and "hardly" correlate with "when", whereas "no sooner" correlates with "than".

q: No sooner had the principal entered the classroom _______ the unruly students fell silent.
exp: "No sooner" is correlatively followed by "than".

q: The doctor advised the diabetic patient to abstain _______ sugary beverages and refined flour.
exp: The verb "abstain" correctly collocates with the preposition "from".

q: The young athlete was disqualified because he was found deficient _______ basic cardiovascular endurance.
exp: The adjective "deficient" takes the preposition "in".

q: The new tax reform policy is detrimental _______ small and medium scale business enterprises.
exp: The adjective "detrimental" collocates with the preposition "to".

q: The reckless driver was impervious _______ repeated warnings from traffic wardens.
exp: "Impervious" takes the preposition "to".

q: He was completely oblivious _______ the impending danger surrounding the campsite.
exp: "Oblivious" takes the preposition "to" or "of".

q: The committee was unanimous _______ its decision to expel the cult members.
exp: "Unanimous" takes the preposition "in" when referring to an action or decision.

q: The defense lawyer argued that the confession was obtained _______ duress.
exp: In legal parlance, an act performed under coercion is done "under duress".

q: The newly inaugurated bridge was named _______ the renowned nationalist hero.
exp: To name someone or something in honor of another person is to name it "after" them.

q: The manager commended the secretary for her unwavering fidelity _______ corporate ethics.
exp: "Fidelity" collocates with "to".

q: She was acquitted and discharged _______ all charges of treasonable felony.
exp: In legal context, one is acquitted "of" a charge.
